units.topic: Use of public AI tools with customer data
units.summary: Employees use free ChatGPT for translations and customer-letter drafting, and the notes record concern that customer data may be pasted into free tools.
units.quote: Several employees use free ChatGPT for translations (Swedish, English, Estonian drivers) and for drafting customer letters. Jari is worried about customer data being pasted into free tools

units.topic: Use of public AI tools with customer data
units.summary: The meeting discussion records concern that the company does not know what customer data employees enter into free AI tools.
units.quote: That worries me a bit, because I have no idea what customer data goes into those tools.

units.summary: The company had no written AI usage policy.
units.quote: there is no AI usage policy yet.

units.time_qualifier: at the time of the document
units.summary: The company had no written policy on the use of generative AI tools.
units.quote: The company has no written policy on the use of generative AI tools.

units.summary: Copilot training had consisted of a one-hour vendor webinar, with no additional guidelines or training.
units.quote: No guidelines or training beyond a one-hour vendor webinar.

units.topic: Personal data in customer service emails
units.summary: Customer service emails contain consumer personal data, including names, phone numbers and home delivery addresses.
units.quote: Emails contain personal data (names, phone numbers, home delivery addresses of consumers for e-commerce customers).

units.summary: For e-commerce customers, the company acts as a data processor under data processing agreements.
units.quote: The company acts as a data processor for its e-commerce customers under data processing agreements.

units.topic: AI Act transparency and data processing
units.summary: The customer service AI discussion raised GDPR questions about where data is processed and AI Act transparency obligations.
units.quote: So there are GDPR questions, where the data is processed, and transparency obligations under the AI Act.

units.topic: AI Act transparency and data processing
units.summary: The notes record questions about who can see customer service data and where it is processed, alongside GDPR and AI Act transparency concerns.
units.quote: GDPR and AI Act transparency questions came up - who can see what, where the data is processed.

units.summary: The overview states that several customer contracts, especially in pharma, restrict transfers of customer data outside the EU/EEA.
units.quote: Several customer contracts (especially in pharma) include clauses restricting the transfer of customer data outside the EU/EEA.

units.summary: The meeting recording states that some pharma customer contracts restrict data transfers outside the EU.
units.quote: some pharma customer contracts restrict data transfers outside the EU.

units.topic: Human review of AI-generated customer replies
units.time_qualifier: at the initial customer service use-case discussion
units.summary: The proposed email triage system would draft replies for an agent to approve; fully automatic replies were not desired at that stage.
units.quote: Not interested in fully automatic replies at this stage.

units.summary: Handwriting was identified as the main risk for freight-document processing and was to be tested on real samples.
units.quote: Handwriting is the main risk; must be tested on real samples.

units.topic: IT capacity and AI solution maintenance
units.summary: The single-person IT function was identified as a bottleneck; any solution needs to be low-maintenance or partner-operated.
units.quote: Risk: single IT person = bottleneck. Any solution must be low-maintenance or partner-operated.

units.summary: The advisors considered forecasting dependent on data quality and said a data extract was needed first.
units.quote: Forecasting is valuable but depends on data quality - need a data extract first.

units.summary: The IT manager was unsure whether pre-2020 WMS data is comparable because the system was replaced or upgraded in 2020.
units.quote: Six years of history exist in the WMS, but the system was replaced/upgraded in 2020 and Jari is not sure whether pre-2020 data is comparable.

units.summary: Customer master data is duplicated between the TMS and Business Central, with no common customer ID.
units.quote: customer master data duplicated between TMS and Business Central; no common customer ID.

units.time_qualifier: at the time of the document
units.summary: The company had not appointed a data protection officer; the CFO was the data protection contact person.
units.quote: the CFO acts as the data protection contact person. No data protection officer has been appointed.

conflicts.description: The company overview says several customer contracts, especially in pharma, restrict transfer of customer data outside the EU/EEA. The meeting recording says some pharma customer contracts restrict data transfers outside the EU. The stated geographic boundary differs; the instructions give no source priority, so the scope of the contractual restriction remains unresolved.
